question: An 18-year-old man comes to the physician because of severe left shoulder pain after a basketball match. During the game, the patient sustained an injury to the posterior part of his outstretched arm after being blocked by a defender. Examination shows no gross deformity of the left shoulder. Palpation of the shoulder elicits mild tenderness. Internal rotation of the arm against resistance shows weakness. These findings are most specific for injury to which of the following muscles?
analysis: The patient's symptoms, particularly the weakness in internal rotation of the arm against resistance, are most indicative of an injury to the subscapularis muscle. The subscapularis is responsible for internal rotation of the shoulder, and weakness in this movement suggests its involvement. The other muscles listed are primarily involved in different movements: the supraspinatus in abduction, the deltoid in abduction and flexion, the infraspinatus in external rotation, and the teres minor in external rotation as well.
